thread:
emily_support: customer (AcmeCorp) reporting Private control plane mTLS failures since their egress upgrade last night. error seen on our side: "tls: bad certificate / handshake failure". they say nothing else changed on our config.
ops-bot: created incident INC-75921 and assigned to support oncall
emily_support: customer says F5 SSL Orchestrator rolled out a new TLS profile on their NAT egress appliances around 23:40 UTC and all their VPC hosts started failing to connect to the private control plane.
rahul_infra: can you get a pcap + openssl s_client -showcerts output from one of their failing hosts? tcpdump on the client and the server side would be ideal.
emily_support: pasted sanitized pcap & openssl output (trimmed) below. key bits: client's Certificate message contains multiple certs (6 total) and size looks large.
-- paste --
openssl s_client -connect cp.private.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=acme-client
 1 s:/CN=acme-intermediate-1
 2 s:/CN=acme-intermediate-2
 3 s:/CN=corp-cross-sig
 4 s:/CN=corp-root-legacy
 5 s:/CN=local-additional-root
---
Certificate chain length (bytes): 18832
---
server TLS log: alert: handshake_failure, peer closed connection
-- end paste --

luis_sre: looking at the pcap: the TLS Certificate message length field is 18832 bytes (Certificate handshake record). Our runtime rejects connection during certificate verify with an internal 'record_overflow' / 'cert_chain_too_large' path. F5 appears to be inserting an extra local root + a cross-signed intermediate, doubling chain size.
rahul_infra: confirmation: our control plane currently has a hard limit for processed certificate chain bytes (~16384) to avoid DoS/memory amplification. Chains > that get dropped early. We do accept client cert + intermediates but not additional customer-managed trust anchors appended by middleboxes.
maya_devops: what's the recommended customer mitigation? they need a quick fix.
rahul_infra: two immediate options for them:
- change the F5 TLS profile from "SSL offload + re-encrypt" to TCP passthrough mode so we see the original client cert chain intact (no insertion), OR
- in the F5 TLS profile disable "Insert CA Certificate" / "Append Root" option (varies by OS). On their BIG-IP TLS profile the setting is under Client SSL > Advanced > Insert CA Certificate = Off.

short-term workaround from our side: we can temporarily increase max_cert_chain_bytes for their control-plane instance, but that has memory/DoS tradeoffs. need eng-runtime approval and a patch to make it per-tenant and rate-limited.
emily_support: customer tried switching to passthrough in a staging NAT and confirmed the handshake completes immediately. they plan to roll the change to prod at 03:00 UTC.
luis_sre: i've filed a follow-up engineering task (ENG-PI-4321) to evaluate dynamic limits and better diagnostics for oversize client chains. adding a telemetry alert to catch Certificate message lengths > 14KB so we can warn earlier.
rahul_infra: repro steps recorded for the ticket:
1) on client host with failing config: run tcpdump -s 0 -w out.pcap host cp.private.redwood.internal and reproduce
2) openssl s_client -connect cp.private.redwood.internal:443 -cert client.pem -key client.key -showcerts -> shows 6 certs
3) observe server response: TLS alert handshake_failure and connection reset

emily_support: customer deployed passthrough change and reports all hosts healthy now. they'll keep F5 team on the hook to fix their TLS profile. recommend KB note and internal runbook entry.
luis_sre: agreed. KB entry suggestion: "F5/SSL Orchestrator inserting local root or intermediate into client cert chain can exceed control-plane chain size limits and break mTLS. Fix: use TLS passthrough or disable 'insert CA' option; if passthrough is impossible, work with eng-runtime for a controlled limit bump." :thumbsup:
emily_support: closing escalation after prod verification. adding links to pcap + openssl excerpts in the incident ticket for postmortem.
